title: Microsoft has a lesson for Apple - Barron's
text:
Microsoft Has a Lesson for Apple By Oct. 3, 2018 10:50 a.m. ET Order Reprints Print Article With its latest Surface line, Microsoft is going to let people pay for devices in installments, similar to how they pay for smartphones. Getty Images Text size
Apple should take a few cues from the way Microsoft is approaching its tablet business.
Microsoft (MSFT) on Tuesday afternoon announced a new line of Surface tablets. There weren’t many surprises for fans of the products. Though Microsoft upgraded its convertible Surface Pro tablet and refreshed the Surface Studio, a tablet intended for painting and design, its more interesting choices have little to do with device specifications.
With its latest Surface line, Microsoft is going to let people pay for devices in installments, similar to how they pay for smartphones. The company’s new All Access program lets consumers finance Surface devices for a starting monthly price of $25, and it throws in an Office 365 subscription as well as “dedicated customer support” services. Newsletter Sign-up
Granted, it’s not a perfect comparison to the smartphone model. Apple’s (AAPL) iPhone Upgrade Program, for example, lets customers pay for their phones in installments but upgrade to a new device yearly after trading in the old one. With Microsoft’s program, users just pay off their new tablet over the course of 24 months.
Still, Apple could learn a few things from Microsoft’s approach, particularly in regards to the bundled Office 365 subscription. As services become a more crucial element of Apple’s overall business, the smartphone maker should look to enhance its iPhone Upgrade Program by adding more service offerings to the upgrade package. It’s an approach that Barron’s has recommended for years .
Apple already includes AppleCare with the upgrade program, but it should consider adding Music and cloud storage, as well. Such services would further tether users to the Apple ecosystem and could help the company compete against Spotify.
Apple didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
If Spotify users were to effectively get a discount on Apple Music by buying it as part of a bundled subscription, some might be tempted to make the switch. Such a program could also help Apple nab customers who don’t yet pay for on-demand music streaming.
The company will probably soon enhance its streaming offerings with more media as it steps up its original-content efforts. “We’ve got great talent in the area that we’ve sourced from different places, and feel really good about what we will eventually offer,” CEO Tim Cook said on Apple’s latest earnings call.
Microsoft has already shown it’s willing to borrow from Apple, introducing Surface headphones as part of Tuesday’s announcements. Apple’s AirPods have been a big win for the company.
